data.name: Chitragupt
data.gender_notes: Chitragupt is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Chitragupta is the god of accounts and records in Hindu mythology. He is often depicted as a young man with a quill in his hand, keeping a record of every person's deeds. In the epic Mahabharata, he is mentioned as the recorder of the deeds of every being in the universe. The name Chitragupt carries the meaning “God of Accounts” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chitragupt usually hope their child will grow to embody god of accounts and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the importance of keeping an accurate record of actions in life.
data.etymology: Chitragupt belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Accounts.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chitragupt total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Chitragupta, as the god of records and Accounts, holds great significance in Hindu culture. He is often invoked during auspicious events such as weddings, housewarming ceremonies, and other important milestones in life, to ensure the event runs smoothly and all related transactions are recorded accurately. The name Chitragupta is also mentioned in various Hindu texts, including the Mahabharata, and features in various stories and mythologies.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Chitragupta represents the idea of accountability and the recording of every act or deed. In Hindu spirituality, it is believed that every action has consequences, and Chitragupta is the one who records and keeps a tally of these deeds. This belief emphasizes the importance of living a virtuous life, as every action has repercussions and will be recorded and weighed in the cosmic scale at the time of death. Chitragupta's name, therefore, serves as a reminder of the spiritual consequences of our actions and the importance of leading a righteous life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chitragupt symbolizes the scribe of cosmic accounts in Hindu mythology. He is the record-keeper of human actions and deeds, overseeing the balance of karma in the cycle of birth and rebirth.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Chitragupt is a god in Hindu mythology. The name Chitragupt carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: He is the god of justice and records.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Chitragupt remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.
